If either amountA or amountB is 0, sqrt returns 0, resulting in negative liquidity (-1000), which is then minted. This violates the invariant that liquidity must be non-negative and leads to invalid pool state.
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: Type System Integrity - Mathematical Domain Validation

vulnerabilities.title: Liquidity Minting with Negative Value Due to sqrt(0)
vulnerabilities.description: In quoteAddLiquidity(), when creating a new pair, liquidity = Math.sqrt(amountA * amountB) - MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY. If amountA or amountB is 0, sqrt returns 0, making liquidity = -1000. This negative value is passed to mint(), which accepts uint and wraps to a huge positive number (2^256 - 1000). This creates a malformed liquidity token with invalid supply, enabling attackers to drain the pool by burning this forged liquidity.
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: Type System Integrity - Mathematical Domain Validation
vulnerabilities.location: quoteAddLiquidity() line: liquidity = Math.sqrt(amountA * amountB) - MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY;

vulnerabilities.title: State Commitment Before Swap Validation in _swapRatio
vulnerabilities.description: In _swapRatio(), the function computes a new balanceA = balanceA - fee and balanceB = balanceB - amountOut, then compares the new k-value against the old. However, this comparison is purely for validation — the actual state (reserves) is never updated in this function. But in swapExactTokensForTokens(), the _safeTransferFrom() is called BEFORE _swap(), meaning tokens are transferred from user to pair even if _swapRatio() would later fail. This commits state (token transfer) before validating swap feasibility, allowing attackers to drain tokens by triggering invalid swaps.
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: Operation Lifecycle Integrity - State Commitment Timing
vulnerabilities.location: swapExactTokensForTokens() calls _safeTransferFrom() before _swap(); _swapRatio() validates but does not modify state

vulnerabilities.title: Authorization Not Bound to Execution Context in Permit-Based Withdrawals
vulnerabilities.description: The permit-based functions (removeLiquidityWithPermit, removeLiquidityETHWithPermit) allow a user to sign a permit for a specific liquidity amount, but the signature does not bind the recipient address or the token pair. An attacker can front-run by submitting the same permit signature with a malicious recipient address (e.g., their own), consuming the permit and withdrawing liquidity to their address instead of the intended recipient. The signature only binds owner, spender, value, and deadline — not the execution context.
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: Operation Lifecycle Integrity - Authorization Context Binding

vulnerabilities.title: Fork Behavioral Divergence: getAmountOut() Assumes Legacy Pair Behavior
vulnerabilities.description: The contract calls IBaseV1Pair(pair).getAmountOut(amountIn, tokenIn) to compute output amounts. However, AlgebraCL (the underlying protocol) uses a different AMM model (concentrated liquidity) where getAmountOut() is deprecated or non-functional. The actual fee calculation and price impact logic is handled by IQuoterV2. Calling getAmountOut() on AlgebraCL pairs returns 0 or garbage, causing getAmountsOut() to incorrectly route trades through invalid pairs, leading to 100% slippage and user funds being trapped.
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: External Integration Integrity - Fork Behavioral Divergence
vulnerabilities.location: getAmountOut(), getAmountsOut() — calls IBaseV1Pair(pair).getAmountOut() on AlgebraCL pairs

vulnerabilities.title: Gas Limit Exploitation in _swap() with Non-Revert Subcalls
vulnerabilities.description: In _swap(), when calling ISwapRouter(swapRouter).exactInputSingle(), the function does not check the return value of the external call. If the subcall fails due to insufficient gas (EVM 63/64 rule) or slippage, it reverts silently, but the parent function continues. This causes the token transfer (via _safeTransferFrom) to occur, but the swap fails — user tokens are sent to the pair, but no output is received. The user loses funds with no recourse.

vulnerabilities.title: Precision Loss in _k() Function for Stable Pairs Due to Truncation
vulnerabilities.description: In _k(), for stable pairs, the function computes _x = x * 1e18 / decimals0 and _y = y * 1e18 / decimals1. This division truncates precision. For example, if x = 1000, decimals0 = 18, then _x = 1000. But if x = 1000000000000000001 (1e18 + 1), _x = 1e18 due to truncation. The product _a * _b then loses the fractional part, causing k-value to be underestimated. This allows attackers to add liquidity with slightly more tokens than allowed, bypassing the k >= k invariant and stealing fee revenue.

vulnerabilities.title: Incorrect Token Balance Calculation in _swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens
vulnerabilities.description: In _swapSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens(), amountInput is computed as erc20(input).balanceOf(address(pair)).sub(reserveInput). However, for fee-on-transfer tokens, the balanceOf() includes the fee that was just transferred in, but the reserveInput is the pre-swap reserve. This double-counts the fee: the fee is already included in balanceOf(), but the swap logic assumes the fee was deducted. This causes the amountOut to be overestimated, leading to underpayment to the next pair and stolen funds.
vulnerabilities.vulnerability_type: Type System Integrity - Value Representation and Comparison
